newsitem.title: UK: World sugar markets could see 98/99 deficit-analyst.
newsitem.headline: World sugar markets could see 98/99 deficit-analyst.

text.p: World sugar markets could enter deficit by 1998/99 if consumption growth continues to accelerate and low prices persuade some key producers to cut output, a leading sugar economist said on Monday.

Sugar output could fall in countries such as Brazil and India if cane was channelled into making other products, said Tony Hannah, chief economist at the London-based International Sugar Organization (ISO).

"Looking forward to 1997/98, the lower prices now prevailing can be expected to trigger the beginning of a production response, especially in those countries like Brazil and India which have an alternative use for cane."
But unless prices fell from current levels, Brazil was likely to continue to expand sugar production but at a slower rate than in the first half of the decade.
Hannah was delivering a prepared speech to the Sixth World Sugar Farmers' Conference in Copenhagen, organised by the World Association of Beet and Cane Growers.
He noted that on the demand side, consumption growth had accelerated from its disappointing average of 1.5 percent of the late 1980s and early 1990s.
"Consequently, the gap between production and consumption may be expected to be closed in 1997/98, with, if past patterns are repeated, a deficit in 1998/99," Hannah said.
"Clearly, once the cumulative surplus is absorbed, prices will again rise."
